title: AGM - Statutory Compliance
description:
Leads HR statutory and labour law compliance for a nationwide branch network: Shops and Establishments, licences, contract labour and the four Labour Codes. A statutory compliance leadership role. Payroll processing sits with a separate payroll team. Job Description / Responsibilities : - PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING : - This is a statutory compliance leadership role in Human Resources. Payroll processing sits with a separate payroll team, and payroll profiles do not match this brief. THE ROLE : - As AGM - Statutory Compliance, you will head HR statutory and labour law compliance for a large, listed NBFC with a nationwide branch network, reporting to the DGM, Human Resources. You will set the compliance standard for every branch and every state, lead the company through the four Labour Codes, and manage the company's relationships with the regulators and vendors this work depends on. The role carries accountability for the company's record with labour, licensing, EPFO, ESIC, professional tax and Labour Welfare Fund authorities across the country. WHY THIS ROLE, NOW : - India's four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, and the central rules followed in May 2026. States are notifying their own rules one by one, so a company operating across many states has to run its state Acts and the new Codes together. This role leads that transition for the whole network. 1. ESTABLISHMENT COMPLIANCE ACROSS THE NETWORK : - Ensure every branch and office holds a valid Shops and Establishments registration, municipal trade licence and the signage and fire clearances its local body requires, renewed and amended on time. Ensure registrations under the OSH Code, professional tax, Labour Welfare Fund and ESIC sub-codes are in place wherever they apply, and stay current as the network grows. Maintain one branch-wise view of every registration, licence, authority and renewal date. 2. BRANCH EXPANSION : - Put a state-wise compliance process in place for branch openings, relocations and closures, so every new branch is registered within the time its state allows. 3. STATUTORY DEPOSITS, RETURNS AND RECORDS : - Ensure every PF, ESI, professional tax and Labour Welfare Fund deposit reaches the right authority on time in every state, working with payroll and local vendors. Ensure every return due under the labour laws is filed on time, and that registers and statutory displays are current at every establishment. 4. REGULATORS AND VENDORS : - Lead the company's engagement with EPFO, ESIC, state labour departments, municipal and fire authorities, and professional tax and Labour Welfare Fund offices. Govern the compliance agents, consultants and service providers who work across the states, and hold them to agreed timelines. 5. CONTRACT STAFF COMPLIANCE : - Own compliance for contract staff across the network, including principal employer registrations and contractors' licences. Put monthly checks in place on contractors' minimum wages and PF and ESI deposits, with paid challans confirmed to Finance before their bills are paid. Ensure state minimum wage notifications reach contractors and are applied. 6. LABOUR CODES : - Lead the company's transition to the four Labour Codes, tracking central and state rules as they are notified. Maintain a live, state-wise gap register and drive the actions it calls for. Work with Payroll, HR Operations and Finance on changes that touch wages, appointment letters, working hours, health check-ups and grievance committees. Lead the move to electronic registers, returns and notices. 7. INSPECTIONS AND NOTICES : - Keep the network inspection ready, and lead the response to inspections, notices and show cause notices, including compounding where it applies. Work with the legal team on disputed matters. 8. GOVERNANCE AND TEAM : - Run the compliance calendar for every branch, state and contractor, and report status to HR leadership every month. Provide the labour, licensing and professional tax inputs for the company's statutory and sustainability disclosures. Lead and develop the statutory compliance team. HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED IN THE FIRST YEAR : - No penalty, fine or prosecution from any labour, licensing, fire, EPFO, ESIC, professional tax or Labour Welfare Fund authority. Every branch holds a valid, displayed registration, trade licence and the local clearances it needs at every point in the year. Every statutory deposit and return reaches the authority on time in every state. Every renewal is filed before expiry, and every new branch is registered within the time its state allows. Every notice is answered within the time allowed and every inspection observation is closed. Every contractor is checked each month, and Finance holds confirmed PF and ESI challans for every contractor bill it pays. The Labour Codes gap register is current for every state, and every newly notified state rule is actioned. Desired profile of the candidate : - NON-NEGOTIABLE A full time, regular postgraduate degree in HR or a closely related field, such as MBA-HR, PGDBM-HR, MSW-HR, or a master's in labour law or labour management. Distance and part time degrees do not qualify. A career in HR statutory and labour law compliance, as the main line of work. WHAT WE ALSO NEED 15 to 23 years in HR. Scale: you have led statutory compliance for at least 300 branches or locations across at least 10 states. Any sector qualifies when this scale is shown on your CV and matches your employer's published branch data. A record of managing regulators and compliance agents across several states. Working knowledge of the four Labour Codes and of where the state rules stand. Based in Chennai, or willing to relocate to Chennai. GOOD TO HAVE A law degree in addition to the postgraduate degree. Experience of audits in an RBI regulated entity. English and Tamil, with Hindi for the northern and central states. PLEASE NOTE This is a statutory compliance leadership role in Human Resources. Payroll processing sits with a separate payroll team. Careers built mainly in payroll processing, administration, facilities or premises management do not match this brief. BE READY TO SPEAK TO NUMBERS The branches or locations, and the states, whose compliance you have led. The registrations and licences obtained or renewed under you in the last twelve months. The contractors and contract staff covered by your compliance checks. The inspections and notices handled under you in the last twelve months, and how they closed. The compliance vendors and agents you govern, and the states they cover. Your current CTC, your notice period and your earliest possible date of joining. Education qualification : - NON-NEGOTIABLE: a full time, regular postgraduate degree in HR or a closely related field, such as MBA-HR, PGDBM-HR, MSW-HR, or a master's in labour law or labour management. Distance and part time degrees do not qualify. A law degree in addition is welcome. Skills : - Statutory Compliance, Labour Law Compliance, HR Statutory Compliance, Establishment Compliance, Labour Codes, Code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Code on Social Security, OSH Code, Shops and Establishments Act, Shop Act Registration, Trade Licence, Trade License, Contract Labour, CLRA, Principal Employer, Contractor Compliance, Vendor Compliance, Minimum Wages Compliance, ESIC Sub Code Registration, Professional Tax Registration, Labour Welfare Fund Registration, Statutory Registers, Labour Returns, Labour Inspections, Show Cause Notice, Compounding, Labour Department, Compliance Calendar, Multi State Compliance, Pan India Compliance, Branch Compliance, NBFC, BFSI, Banking, Financial Services Location of job posting : - Chennai, corporate office. Candidates based in Chennai, or willing to relocate to Chennai.

Key Skills: Statutory Compliance,HR Statutory Compliance,Trade License,Labour Codes,Shop Act Registration,Labour Law Compliance,OSH Code,Code on Wages

Senior Manager - Corporate Legal and Commercial Affairs
Senior Manager Legal litigation and corporate affairs
description:
Role & responsibilities 
 Corporate Lawyer Litigation & Compliance Industry: Manufacturing / Automotive / Engineering
 Experience: 10–15 Years
 Employment Type: Full-time
 Function: Legal & Corporate Affairs
 Location: Chennai, Tamil Nadu
 Employer: Leading Manufacturing Organization Role Overview We are looking for an accomplished Corporate Lawyer with 10–15 years of experience to join the legal team of a large, established manufacturing organization. The role requires a strong combination of litigation management, regulatory and statutory compliance, corporate legal advisory, and stakeholder management . The successful candidate should have substantial in-house legal experience within a manufacturing, automotive, engineering, industrial, or allied organization and be comfortable handling complex legal matters across multiple business functions and locations. Key Responsibilities Litigation Management Manage civil, commercial, consumer, labour, employment and other litigation involving the organization. Handle matters before courts, tribunals, statutory authorities and other judicial/quasi-judicial forums. Coordinate closely with external advocates, law firms and senior counsels for ongoing litigation. Prepare and review notices, replies, pleadings, affidavits, petitions and other litigation-related documentation. Track litigation matters, legal exposures, hearing dates, outcomes and action points. Develop litigation strategy in consultation with internal stakeholders and external counsel. Drive timely closure and resolution of disputes while protecting the organization's legal and commercial interests. Manage pre-litigation disputes and support negotiation, mediation and settlement wherever appropriate. Compliance & Regulatory Ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations and statutory requirements relevant to manufacturing operations. Monitor changes in legislation and assess their impact on the business. Work with business functions to strengthen the organization's compliance framework. Support periodic legal and compliance audits across functions and locations. Identify compliance gaps and recommend appropriate corrective and preventive actions. Maintain appropriate compliance documentation, records and reporting mechanisms. Partner with internal stakeholders on implementation of policies, SOPs and statutory requirements. Support interactions with government departments, regulators and statutory authorities wherever required. Corporate Legal Advisory Provide practical legal advice to business teams on day-to-day operational and commercial matters. Advise management on legal risks arising from business decisions, operational issues and disputes. Review and interpret applicable legislation, regulatory requirements and contractual obligations. Support senior leadership in evaluating legal exposure and developing appropriate risk-mitigation strategies. Provide legal guidance to HR, procurement, operations, finance, sales and other business functions. Contracts & Documentation Review, draft and negotiate commercial agreements, vendor agreements, service agreements, NDAs, purchase arrangements and other business contracts. Identify contractual risks and recommend appropriate safeguards. Standardize legal clauses and documentation wherever possible. Support contractual dispute resolution and enforcement matters. Legal Governance & Risk Management Maintain dashboards/MIS for litigation, compliance and critical legal matters. Identify emerging legal and regulatory risks affecting the organization. Support development and strengthening of internal legal governance mechanisms. Ensure appropriate documentation, approvals and legal controls are maintained for material matters. Work closely with senior management on high-impact and sensitive legal issues. Candidate Profile The ideal candidate should have: 10–15 years of post-qualification legal experience. Significant experience working as an in-house legal professional in a manufacturing organization . Strong hands-on exposure to litigation and dispute management . Demonstrated experience in statutory, regulatory and corporate compliance . Good understanding of laws relevant to industrial and manufacturing organizations. Experience coordinating with external advocates, law firms, regulatory authorities and senior internal stakeholders. Strong ability to assess legal risk and translate legal requirements into practical business recommendations. Excellent drafting, negotiation, analytical and communication skills. Ability to independently manage multiple high-priority legal matters. Preferred Industry Background Candidates from the following sectors will be particularly relevant: Automotive / Auto Components Heavy Engineering Industrial Manufacturing Engineering & Capital Goods Machinery / Equipment Manufacturing Metals / Steel Chemicals Consumer Durables Electrical / Electronics Manufacturing Other large manufacturing organizations Candidates whose experience is predominantly with law firms, consulting organizations, IT/ITES, banking or financial services without meaningful manufacturing-sector exposure may not be aligned with the role. Educational Qualification LL.B. from a recognized university is mandatory. LL.M. or additional qualifications in corporate/commercial law will be an advantage. Key Competencies Litigation & Dispute Management Legal Compliance Regulatory Affairs Corporate Law Manufacturing Laws & Regulations Commercial Contracts Legal Risk Management Legal Drafting Stakeholder Management External Counsel Management Negotiation Legal Governance What We Are Looking For This opportunity will suit a legal professional who combines strong legal fundamentals with commercial judgment and is capable of operating effectively within a complex manufacturing environment. The individual should be able to independently manage litigation and compliance matters while serving as a trusted legal advisor to senior business stakeholders. 
 Preferred candidate profile

Key Skills: Arbitration,Corporate Governance,Litigation,Legal,Litigation management,Corporate affairs,Governance,Corporate
